Lessons.Title: Multiply Multiples of Ten
ExplanationParagraphs: An original base-ten rod has ten ones. Grouping rods makes multiplication by a multiple of ten easier: (a×b)×10=a×(b×10). A product above100 is still counting groups of tens.

Original warm-up source diagram has TWELVE tens rods arranged as four rows of three:120;3×40=4×30=12×10=120. This original source image was visually read, first-party independent models preserve row/group math.

Activity1 A Whole Lot of Dollars: six friends start with $100 each; play bills are $5,$10,$20,$50,$100. Original options: one $100=100 YES, four $20=80 NO, ten $10=100 YES, ten $5=50 NO, five $20=100 YES, twenty $10=200 NO, twenty $5=100 YES, two $50=100 YES.

Noah pays Lin$150 with SAME-TYPE bills. All options among available denominations are thirty $5, fifteen $10 or three $50. A whole number of twenties or hundreds cannot total $150. Explain why via division and dollars.

Source final balances: Andre9×10+10×5=140; Clare14×10=140; Jada10×10+3×50=250; Lin8×20=160; Noah6×50=300; Tyler21×10=210. Noah wins with$300; the tie at$140 between Andre and Clare is not a winning tie.
Activity2 Two Strategies uses second original diagram 24 ten rods arranged in eight rows of three:8×30=240. Jada counts30,60,90,120,150,180,210,240. Kiran sees8×3=24 tens, so24×10=240.
Original source expressions:5×60=300,8×50=400,4×30=120,7×40=280,9×20=180. Verify place value, not just add a zero by rote.

Teacher checks money representations, alternative strategies and group discussion. No publisher original SVG art, source student PDF or gated What's the Value? Cool-down copied. No Stage D, runtime test or academic approval.
